question: Ford spent $250 million on the Edsel before its 1957 launch, then sold about 110,000 in two years. Was market research to blame?
answer: Not as the legend says. Brooks found the motivational research came after the car was designed, only to shape its advertising. What sank the Edsel was a pile-up: record hype, then early cars with oil leaks, sticking hoods and trunks that would not open, and a recession with buyers turning to small, plain cars.
move: When a failure has one neat explanation, look for the causes it hides.
simply: If a cake flops, it is tempting to blame the new recipe. But maybe the oven was broken, the eggs were old and nobody was hungry that day.
why: Post-mortems at work and in the news like one tidy cause. Fix the wrong one and the next launch fails the same way: dropping research would not have saved the Edsel; better quality control and timing might have.
